title: Why I Automate Everything I Can
description: Some thoughts on building workflow automations and what I learned shipping them for clients.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Automation changes the way I work because it reduces repetitive effort and gives me more time to focus on decisions that actually move projects forward.

When a task repeats often enough, it becomes a candidate for automation. The goal is not to remove human judgment, but to remove the mechanical work that slows us down.

sections.title: Process
sections.content:
I start by mapping the workflow and identifying which steps are repetitive, fragile, or easy to forget. Once those steps are clear, I look for a small automation that removes friction without making the system harder to understand.

This usually means writing a few reliable rules, connecting APIs carefully, and keeping a human review point where the outcome matters most.

sections.title: Lessons
sections.content:
The biggest lesson is that automation works best when it is boring, visible, and easy to change. If the system is difficult to explain, it will be difficult to trust.

Good automation is not about doing more with less; it is about doing the right things with fewer interruptions and less risk of error.

title: Deploying a Vite Portfolio to GitHub Pages
description: A practical guide to running, building, and deploying this React portfolio with GitHub Pages.

sections.title: The npm Commands
sections.content:
npm run dev starts Vite's local development server. Use it while writing code because it provides fast hot reloads and lets you test the portfolio at a local URL. It is intended for development and is not the command that publishes the site.

npm run build creates the optimized production files in the dist folder. Use it to check that the app compiles successfully and to prepare the files that a hosting service will publish.

npm run preview serves the finished dist folder locally. Use it after npm run build when you want to test the production version before deploying it.

npm run deploy runs npm run build and then uses gh-pages to push dist to the gh-pages branch. This is the command that updates the live GitHub Pages site.

sections.title: GitHub Pages Deployment
sections.content:
Before deploying, make sure vite.config.js uses the repository base path, such as /portfolio/. Public assets should use relative paths like resume.pdf and certifications/example.jpg so they work under that base path.

Push the source code to GitHub, then run npm run deploy. The gh-pages package publishes the generated dist folder to the gh-pages branch. In the repository settings, open Pages and choose Deploy from a branch, select gh-pages, and use the root folder.

The live URL is usually https://your-username.github.io/your-repository/. The first deployment can take a short time to become available.

sections.title: Updating the Site
sections.content:
After making changes, run npm run build to catch production errors. Commit and push the source changes with git add ., git commit, and git push. Then run npm run deploy to publish the new dist output.

The normal update flow is: edit the site, test with npm run dev, verify with npm run build, push the source code, and deploy with npm run deploy.

tabs.title: Quick Reference
tabs.content:
npm run dev = local development server

npm run build = production build in dist

npm run preview = preview the production build locally

npm run deploy = build and publish dist to GitHub Pages

tabs.title: Git Checklist
tabs.content:
1. Commit and push source changes.

2. Confirm the Vite base path matches the repository name.

3. Run npm run deploy.

4. Confirm GitHub Pages uses the gh-pages branch.
